SectionPath: Why does my HTML content look different than what I previewed locally?
Blocks.Text: The difference you're seeing is likely due to variations in rendering engines. Local preview depends on your browser and environment, which may render styles and elements differently than LinkedIn's platform.

Blocks.Section: Is there a character limit for the job description field?
SectionPath: Is there a character limit for the job description field?
Blocks.Text: Yes, there is a 25,000-character limit for the job description field on LinkedIn. This limit applies to all jobs posted on the platform.

Blocks.Section: Is there a character limit for the job description field?
SectionPath: Is there a character limit for the job description field?
Blocks.Text: Important: This character count excludes HTML tags—only the visible text content is counted toward the limit.

Blocks.Section: Why is the styling different for job postings when viewed signed in versus not signed in?
SectionPath: Why is the styling different for job postings when viewed signed in versus not signed in?
Blocks.Text: Layout differences can occur because job descriptions are rendered differently depending on whether the viewer is signed in or not. This is due to different rendering engines used for each experience.

This section provides answers to common questions about HTML formatting and styling in job postings.
The list of supported HTML tags can be found in our job posting API schema documentation.
LinkedIn doesn't recommend using HTML/CSS tags other than the supported ones. While certain attribute tags such as <a href=''> may be accepted, they are not guaranteed to work as expected.
LinkedIn doesn't recommend using styling-related tags, as they may not render consistently.
LinkedIn doesn't recommend using HTML/CSS tags beyond those specifically listed in our supported HTML tags documentation.
While some unlisted tags might appear to work, there's no guarantee they will be supported consistently. Unsupported tags may be:

Stripped out entirely
Rendered as plain text
Lead to unpredictable formatting or display issues

The difference you're seeing is likely due to variations in rendering engines. Local preview depends on your browser and environment, which may render styles and elements differently than LinkedIn's platform.
LinkedIn's rendering engine is optimized for:

Consistency across devices and browsers
Security and safety
Performance

This means certain HTML tags or styles might be interpreted differently compared to local browser behavior. Additionally, some CSS or browser-specific behavior won't carry over to LinkedIn's environment.
Best practices:

Stick to the supported HTML tags
Keep tags as simple as possible
Contact the tech support team if you encounter unexpected or confusing output
Yes, there is a 25,000-character limit for the job description field on LinkedIn. This limit applies to all jobs posted on the platform.
Important: This character count excludes HTML tags—only the visible text content is counted toward the limit.

Layout differences can occur because job descriptions are rendered differently depending on whether the viewer is signed in or not. This is due to different rendering engines used for each experience.
While aiming for consistency, some minor formatting differences may occur due to:

Different rendering engines for signed-in vs. non-signed-in users
Different experiences provided for each user state
What to do:

If the differences aren't causing issues, no action is needed
If specific layout or style problems are affecting readability, please report them with details
The more detail provided, the better the possible solutions can be explored
LinkedIn values your feedback and is available to help if anything becomes disruptive.
